The national-framework page this record stands under: the parent nation legalised same-sex marriage and full adoption in 2013 (civil solidarity pacts since 1999), the penal code has covered 'gender identity' since an 18 November 2016 amendment that replaced 'sexual identity' (protected since 2012), and homophobic hate speech has carried penalties up to EUR 45,000 and/or one year's imprisonment since a 31 December 2004 amendment. On legal gender recognition, a bill approved by the legislature was signed into law on 18 November 2016 and took effect on 1 January 2017: it abolished the sex-reassignment-surgery and forced-sterilisation requirements, rejected a proposal that would have demanded proof of medical treatment, and requires going before a court rather than any medical intervention; transsexualism is classed under a long-term-illness category, so gender-affirming treatment is funded by the national medical-insurance scheme. It supplies the concrete national rules on documents, protection and care that a trans visitor encounters and grounds the record's at-national-score assessment, since the regional page carries no trans-specific content.
